overall: Violation found: the Board failed to give the subject of a Purpose One executive session written notice, but the AG found the violation unintentional and cured by open-session discussion and apology; Board ordered to comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Complainant, a selectman, said the Board discussed a complaint against him in executive session on July 6, 2010 without written notice that he was the subject.
allegations.key_passage: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law on July 6, 2010 by failing to notify the subject of an executive session under Purpose One, resulting in a denial of the rights afforded to you under G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(1).

allegations.summary: Complainant disputed the accuracy of the July 6, 2010 executive session minutes and sought amendments; the Board adopted his proposed amendments in open session on August 17.
allegations.key_passage: a reading of the executive session minutes and your suggested amendments to the executive session minutes, which were then adopted by the Board

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the provisions of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25.
remedy_passage: we find that the Board took appropriate steps to cure the violation, and order immediate and future compliance with the provisions of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25.
